title: These tech outages are giving Y2K, AI agent style
lede: A run of US outages, from Apple Pay to an FAA ground stop, has security figures arguing that AI-speed vulnerability discovery and rushed patching, not attacks, may be the common thread.

points: Within two weeks Apple Pay, NASA's internal network, the FAA and Microsoft's Outlook, Teams and Copilot all went down.
Officials and most of the affected companies say the incidents were technical failures rather than cyberattacks.
Investor Dave DeWalt argues AI tools are surfacing old flaws so quickly that the scramble to patch them is causing short-term breakage.
Corsha founder Anusha Iyer blames hasty mixing of modern systems with legacy hardware, citing early findings on the FAA's telecom upgrade.
Both urge more testing, tighter segmentation and phased rollouts; DeWalt expects new startups in automated remediation and safe patch deployment.

sections.text: If AI is speeding up how fast flaws are found, the bottleneck shifts to testing and shipping fixes safely, especially where new code meets legacy systems that cannot keep pace.
